summary:
Observed in review of FS.GG.SDD `upgrade` owner-skill replacement (FS-GG/FS.GG.SDD#1155, merged as #1158); the rule below is the one merged in FS-GG/FS.GG.SDD#1161.

**The rule as first merged (#1158).** A skill with no recorded owner-package version (a record that predates version tracking) was replaced when the running CLI was not older than the CLI that last wrote the workspace. Equal was allowed on purpose, so the run that finishes an interrupted refresh, or one after the user reverted an edit, is not stranded.

**Why it was wrong.** An equal version string proves nothing: two builds can share it. The reviewer ran a 2.5.4 dev build carrying FS.GG.Drivers 0.97.1 against a workspace a 2.5.4 had produced with the 0.98 pack, and it replaced an untouched 0.98 skill with the older pack. A bound on the CLI's version says nothing about the PACK it carries.

**The merged rule (#1161).** For a skill with no recorded version both bounds must hold. (1) A channel floor: the pack is not below the highest version the record already holds for that channel; this is a fact about the workspace and also catches the dev build. (2) A writer bound: the CLI is strictly newer than the CLI that last wrote the workspace (`upgradedBy`, recorded only by an upgrade in which every file landed, else the producing CLI), or equal to it only when `upgradedBy` names this very CLI, so a complete run of this release already vouched for the workspace and this run can finish what an edit, a link or a read-only directory blocked. A partial run does not record `upgradedBy`, or it would bar its own completion. A malformed version entry is kept and holds, never silently dropped. Measured: the same dev build now does nothing to that workspace and its `work-board` is byte-identical before and after.

**Scope.** Owner-sourced skills in `upgrade`. Package versions are compared by numeric core; a prerelease suffix does not order. The cited source is the merged state at 4b54aa17; verify the current rule against OwnerSkillRefresh.fs on main.
title: A never-downgrade bound that treats an equal CLI version as safe is defeated by a dev build with an older pack
